_comment: Tier-1 static regression checks. Pure substring grep over repo files — zero model tokens, deterministic, run on every change. 'forbidden' patterns must not appear (optionally limited by 'in' path-substring); 'required' patterns must appear in the file(s) whose path contains 'in'. These encode PROJECT CONVENTIONS, some of which are stricter than raw SAP rules (noted per rule).

rules.note: Project convention: RAP audit 'created at' is a timestamp -> @Semantics.systemDateTime.createdAt. @Semantics.systemDate.* is valid in SAP only for genuine date-only fields; do not use it for audit semantics here. (grounding-protocol.md is excluded: it discusses this very anti-pattern as a worked example.)
Same convention as createdAt: audit 'last changed at' is a timestamp -> @Semantics.systemDateTime.lastChangedAt.
The annotations reference must teach the correct timestamp audit annotation.
RAP projection contract must be documented.
The unmanaged/additional save saver base class must be documented.
xsdbool vs boolc guidance must be present.
ABAP SQL test double must be documented.
The MOVE-CORRESPONDING-vs-CORRESPONDING# BASE trap must be documented.
The reference must document that @Semantics.systemDate.* is for date-only fields (not a blanket 'never systemDate'); systemDateTime is the RAP audit-timestamp standard.

The action skill must warn that COMMIT ENTITIES/COMMIT WORK inside a handler or saver dumps with this runtime error (grounded: github.com/SAP-samples/abap-cheat-sheets 17_SAP_LUW.md, 'modify transactional phase' example).

Project convention: when a RAP action needs to modify AND commit another BO independently, teach the CL_ABAP_PARALLEL isolation pattern (own aRFC session/LUW) alongside same-LUW EML (default) and bgPF (after-commit async).
The parallel-processing skill must document the RAP commit-isolation use case (committing another BO from a behavior implementation via a worker task) with its consistency caveat.
Publishing convention: skills/agents/docs must cite public GitHub URLs (github.com/SAP-samples/...), never the local example/ mirror folder — it is deleted before the repo is published.

Publishing convention: no machine-local absolute paths (a Windows user-profile directory) in published content; cite public URLs instead. Pattern is drive-and-user agnostic so it catches any contributor's path, and embeds no real username.
Root CLAUDE.md must wire the superpowers development loop (brainstorming stage marker). Covered via scanFiles since CLAUDE.md lives outside scanDirs.

rules.pattern: Your place in the development process
rules.note: The developer agent must carry the stage-note subsection tying it to the superpowers development loop.

rules.pattern: Always load `abap-clean-style` before generating any ABAP
rules.note: Project policy: abap-clean-style is loaded unconditionally before any ABAP generation, not only when the task maps to the style row. Locked after a review found the load was conditional and single-letter identifiers slipped into generated code.

A bare COMMIT ENTITIES with no RESPONSE OF/FAILED/REPORTED discards the outcome and models committing without asserting anything. Where a test genuinely needs to cross the save sequence (e.g. testing an on-save determination), use COMMIT ENTITIES RESPONSE OF ... FAILED ... REPORTED ... and assert on the result, as in determine_sets_audit_fields_on_save.

Managed numbering keys are available in MAPPED without a commit; committing here only to read failed_commit/reported_commit models an unnecessary commit in a test. A test that genuinely needs to assert a save-sequence outcome should use a distinctly-named FAILED/REPORTED target (e.g. failed_save) scoped to that specific test.

Hashed-table traversal order is unspecified/implementation-defined per the ABAP Keyword Documentation, not a guaranteed insertion order. Use a sorted table or an explicit secondary sorted key when order matters.
Same convention as internal-tables-no-hashed-insertion-order-claim, locking references/operations.md's differently-worded (pre-fix) phrasing of the same claim.
assert_text_matches is a real cl_abap_unit_assert method (see references/assert-cheatsheet.md); SKILL.md previously denied its existence, contradicting the cheatsheet in the same skill.
MAX(key)+index numbering is racy under concurrent saves. Use cl_numberrange_runtime=>number_get (see rap-saves-and-numbering's late-numbering-adjust-numbers.abap) instead of a demo MAX-based pattern.
